question: Which federal bodies were created, cut, restructured or restored in 2025-26?
answer: The federal tree records 32 bodies changed in 2025-26: 9 newly chartered, 1 re-established without legal continuity, 6 restructured, 4 restored by the courts, 11 being wound up and 1 proposed with no legal entity yet.

items.title: Presidential Working Group on Digital Asset Markets
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Office of the President › National Economic Council
items.text: EO 14178 interagency policy body for digital assets, stablecoins, market structure, and the proposed stockpile.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
Advisory and coordinating authority; its report does not itself create a regulator, charter, transaction, or custody transfer.

items.title: Task Force to Eliminate Fraud
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Office of the President
items.text: EO 14395 interagency task force chaired by the Vice President for benefit-program identity, eligibility, pre-payment, and fraud controls.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
The body exists, but its complete 30-, 60-, and 90-day outputs have not been located publicly; coordination is not an adjudication that fraud occurred.

items.title: Stablecoin Certification Review Committee (SCRC)
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of the Treasury
items.text: GENIUS Act committee of the Treasury Secretary, Federal Reserve Chair, and FDIC Chair for state stablecoin-regime certification and specified interpretive rules.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
A statutory interagency gate; a proposed framework or existing state license is not a final Committee certification.

items.title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Permanent Treasury-held BTC reserve, chartered by EO, seeded with forfeited bitcoin. Still fighting to become statute.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
Holds real assets before its articles are fully signed — the loudest tell in the whole stack.

items.title: US Digital Asset Stockpile
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Sister vehicle holding non-bitcoin forfeited digital assets under Treasury.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
A second new Treasury sub-ledger created the same day.

items.title: Administration for a Healthy America
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Health & Human Services
items.text: New HHS entity that absorbed SAMHSA and parts of HRSA in 2025.
kv: The fresh charter built out of wound-up subsidiaries.

items.title: Science, Technology, and Innovation Board
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Defense › Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering
items.text: DoD science, technology, and innovation advisory body with current taskings and meeting records.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

Its charter and establishment notice say it incorporates the missions of the Defense Innovation Board and Defense Science Board. Mission incorporation is not proof of legal continuity or of either predecessor's completed termination filing.

items.title: US Investment Accelerator
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Commerce
items.text: New Commerce office (EO 14255) to fast-track $1B+ investments — the real mechanism behind the decentralized 'sovereign wealth fund'.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
Instead of one fund entity, the state invests through this office, deal by deal. The vehicle hides in an office.

items.title: US Sovereign Wealth Fund
items.sub: Executive Branch
items.text: Directed by EO Feb 2025; a plan was delivered, but no single legal entity was stood up. It went decentralized — stakes taken agency by agency, largely through the Commerce Investment Accelerator.
kv: The purest case of the theory: not one fund but a MODE — money and mandate moving through many vehicles, none of which is 'the fund.' Dashed because it has no body of its own.

items.title: President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST, EO 14177)
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Office of the President
items.text: The current presidential science-and-technology advisory council created by EO 14177.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

A new legal identity, not uninterrupted continuation of the EO 14007 council. DOE funds and administratively and technically supports it but does not own it. Appointments were announced 25 Mar 2026; no meeting or output of this identity was verified through the 28 Sep 2026 cutoff. The order terminates the council 23 Jan 2027 unless extended.

items.title: DOGE
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Office of the President
items.text: Department of Government Efficiency — a re-flagged US Digital Service (USDS, 2014), re-chartered to run the dissolutions.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
The instrument of the reorg is itself a re-chartered entity. It eats from inside the org chart.

items.title: Dept of State
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments
items.text: Absorbed USAID's surviving functions in 2025 after that agency was cut ~95%.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
Classic absorption — a dissolved sibling's remnants roll up into a survivor.

items.title: Dept of Health & Human Services
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments
items.text: Reorganized in 2025 — sub-agencies dissolved and rolled into a new survivor (HEW, 1953).
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: Dept of Homeland Security
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments
items.text: Internal offices shut down March 2025 (Civil Rights & Civil Liberties, two ombudsmen).
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: US Institute of Peace
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Foreign aid & influence
items.text: Targeted Feb 2025. A district court ruled for USIP in May 2025, but the D.C. Circuit stayed that ruling on June 27, 2025. Its website now presents it as the 'Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace'.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: Woodrow Wilson International Center
items.sub: Federally chartered / quasi-official › Smithsonian Institution
items.text: A Smithsonian-affiliated think tank — hit in 2025, core functions preserved; running fellowships again by spring 2026.

items.title: Office for Civil Rights & Civil Liberties
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Homeland Security
items.text: Shut down March 2025 (~500 investigations frozen) — then RESTORED: DHS reversed the closure; reopened by March 2026.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: Federal Mediation & Conciliation Service
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Labor, personnel & retirement
items.text: Named for elimination March 2025 — courts vacated the shutdown (Dec 2025); staff reinstated, fully operational again.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: Institute of Museum & Library Services
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Culture, knowledge & service
items.text: Named for elimination March 2025; government withdrew its appeal in the Apr 2026 settlement — staff returned, agency restored.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
A contested dissolution — the entity fought back and won.

items.title: Inter-American Foundation
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Foreign aid & influence
items.text: Gutted Feb 2025; reinstated by court. The D.C. Circuit denied the government's request to pause that order on June 5, 2025 (Aviel v. Gor); the appeal's final outcome is not yet checked.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: CDFI Fund
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Channels capital into community development financial institutions — named for reduction March 2025.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: USAID (remnant)
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of State
items.text: Cut ~95%; what survived was folded into State.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: SAMHSA
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Health & Human Services
items.text: Dissolved March 2025 ($8.1B, ~900 staff) into the new AHA.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: HRSA (parts)
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Health & Human Services
items.text: Partly dissolved / rolled into AHA.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: Dept of Education
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments
items.text: Marked for wind-down in 2025; functions being dispersed to other departments.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
The status flag records the project and campaign state. The statutory department remains legally active unless Congress changes the law.

items.title: Minority Business Development Agency
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of Commerce
items.text: Named for elimination March 2025.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: CFPB
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Financial regulators
items.text: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — funding cut off and gutted in 2025.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
Starved, not abolished: the shell survives while the function is hollowed.

items.title: AmeriCorps (CNCS)
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Culture, knowledge & service
items.text: The national-service agency — RIF'd April 2025; June 2025 injunction restored programs in plaintiff states only.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements
One entity, one story: a contested dissolution, unresolved — discovery runs to Sep 2026, motions due 2027. (Was listed three ways with three flags; reconciled.)

items.title: US Agency for Global Media
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Foreign aid & influence
items.text: Runs Voice of America — named for elimination March 2025.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: US African Development Foundation
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Foreign aid & influence
items.text: Staff and grants stripped 2025; slated out of the 2026 budget.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: US Interagency Council on Homelessness
items.sub: Executive Branch › Independent agencies & regulators › Oversight & small commissions
items.text: Named for elimination March 2025.
kv: Consolidated: counted in the audited U.S. financial statements

items.title: External Revenue Service (proposed)
items.sub: Executive Branch › Executive Departments › Dept of the Treasury
items.text: Announced to collect tariffs and foreign-source revenue — but it cannot be created without Congress, so as of 2026 it is a name, not an entity.
kv: A proposal clock, not a founding clock. Dashed because no statutory body has been created.

uncertain: Most statuses date from the July 25, 2026 whole-federal sweep and the tree's later notes; a card shows its own check date where the status was rechecked against an official record.

A status marks the tree's latest reading. Court cases can turn again on appeal, so a 'restored' or 'being wound up' body can change; the cards say when a status was last checked against the court's own orders.
'Re-established without legal continuity' means a body with the same name was set up again, not that the old one survived.
sources: The federal tree: masters/federal_entities.json (DR-104), status field and its sources.

catalog_context.title: One map to browse all saved federal research
catalog_context.answer: This is a navigation hub, not a finding: it puts Katie's saved government research, a map of federal bodies, congressional committees, confirmed changes and known gaps in one place, while keeping each source's evidence separate.

catalog_context.title: What changed in the federal government, October 3–12
catalog_context.answer: Treasury put a new payment check into operation, bank regulators imposed joined orders on separate American Express companies, GAO found two unlawful impoundments, and the President opened a formal Federal Reserve removal inquiry.
